A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Discrete Diffusion VLA. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original LIBERO and SimplerEnv evaluations, OOD tests, decoding ablations, and inference measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains original simulation results and adds physical-robot trials and a controlled action-head comparison using Qwen2.5-VL.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 removes the residual-drop check and its cached reference confidences. Secondary re-masking now uses only the absolute-confidence threshold. The main backbone, action tokenization, masked cross-entropy objective, and adaptive refinement procedure are retained.

E1.justification: v4 adds RoboTwin simulation demonstrations and physical AgileX Cobot Magic training and evaluation for clicking a bell and placing a cup on a coaster (Section 4.6). This substantially extends coverage to physical deployment. Existing LIBERO, SimplerEnv, and OOD coverage remains; the Qwen ablation uses existing LIBERO suites.

E2.justification: v4 adds OpenVLA-OFT (L1) to standard LIBERO and both OOD comparisons (Tables 1–3). Appendix F also introduces controlled Qwen2.5-VL versions of AR, parallel decoding, FAST, and GR00T-style diffusion heads. These materially expand comparison against the proposed decoder; SimplerEnv comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include staged real-robot training with 150 simulation demonstrations for 80k steps, then 150 physical demonstrations for 200k steps, chunk size 12, and 15 trials per task. Appendix F jointly trains all four LIBERO suites for 30k steps from Qwen2.5-VL initialization. These are added experimental designs; the original simulation settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a controlled action-head ablation testing whether gains depend on robot pretraining. Conversely, v3 Table 6's separate secondary-re-masking condition and its reported 0.4-point benefit disappear from v4 Table 7. Temperature and denoising-step analyses also receive revised results.

E5.justification: v3 specifies no repeated-run count. v4 Appendix C newly states three random seeds and mean reporting, while Table 1 instead specifies the highest score across seeds. Thus reporting expands but aggregation remains inconsistent. No confidence intervals or run-level dispersion are added, and an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Reported LIBERO average changes from 96.3% to 96.4%; Object changes 98.6→99.4, Goal 97.4→96.8, and Long 92.0→92.2. Goal OOD success remains 96.0%/76.4%, so smaller degradation figures reflect the lower ID score. The diffusion baseline's Spatial OOD scores change from 95.2%/94.6% to 94.3%/91.1%; ablation and step-sweep values also change. New entries include L1 comparisons, 66.7% bell and 40.0% cup success (Table 9), and a 95.1% Qwen action-head average (Table 13). SimplerEnv scores and the main latency table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.5 removes the mathematical definitions of reference confidence, confidence residual, the residual-drop set, and its union with threshold-based re-masking. The forward/reverse diffusion formulation and masked loss remain. New explicit sampling and inference equations largely formalize existing descriptions; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3's overall LIBERO SOTA claim is narrowed to best among discrete methods, acknowledging OpenVLA-OFT (L1) at 97.1% versus 96.4%. v4 adds physical-robot validation to its main contributions and strengthens the conclusion to claim prior preservation 'by construction' and elimination of compounding errors.

C2.justification: v4 introduces competing gradients as the explanation for continuous diffusion's loss of VLM priors and attributes the remaining LIBERO gap to quantization. Appendices E–F expand architectural interpretations and claim an intrinsic decoding advantage independent of robot pretraining. Variable-length tokenization incompatibility becomes an explicit limitation. v3's PaliGemma-based explanation of language sensitivity is removed.

D1.justification: v4 adds comparison-specific result provenance, reproduction hardware, batch sizes, and budgets (Appendix C), a complete OOD instruction list (Table 11), and implementation settings for the new experiments. Existing implementation details largely move from Appendix C to B. However, v3's abstract code-access link is removed without a replacement.

R1.justification: Citations add PaliGemma, Qwen3-VL, SkillDiffuser, Hume, and two Fang works, while removing LAPA, DexVLA, and multi-token prediction. v4 explicitly acknowledges that AR already provides architectural unification, refining the earlier novelty framing. Numerous other reference changes are publication updates to the same works.

P1.justification: The introduction, architecture explanation, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. LIBERO performance and retention are combined, platform evaluations and analysis sections are reorganized, and appendices are restructured. Existing decoding discussion is consolidated into the main text; the LLM-use disclosure is removed and limitations and impact statements are added.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 is redrawn, the old benchmark montage is removed, and real-robot imagery and several tables are added. Table 1 now groups continuous versus discrete methods. Figure 6 is rearranged and its frequency listing shortened; Appendix Table 12 redisplays existing OOD degradation results.

improvement.justification: The added L1 comparator and narrower LIBERO claim make comparisons more credible. The Qwen ablation, physical trials, and provenance disclosures provide useful additional support. The net improvement is limited by contradictory seed aggregation, removal of the direct re-masking ablation and code link, and stronger causal claims about guaranteed prior preservation that the experiments do not directly establish.
